title: Single-shot on-chip measurement of the modal Stokes parameters
summary: Integrated photonics has recently facilitated manipulating multimode partially coherent light in a compact mesh of Mach-Zehnder interferometers. A critical task in this context is on-chip reconstruction of the coherence matrix through a sequence of measurement configurations, thus giving rise to a speed bottleneck stemming from temporal delays in tuning on-chip phase shifts. Here we demonstrate single-shot reconstruction of the coherence matrix for two-mode partially coherent light by parallelizing the on-chip measurements of the modal Stokes parameters, thereby exchanging space for time. Although a larger chip area is required, the reconstruction is limited only by detection speed, thus potentially paving the way to real-time reconstruction of coherence matrices for applications in high-speed communications, cryptography, computation, and sensing.

title: Supersymmetry of Helmholtz waves
summary: Symmetry organizes physical laws, links conservation principles to transformations, and reveals connections between seemingly different systems. We show that Helmholtz waves support Witten supersymmetry through their spatial symmetries, without additional internal degrees of freedom. Reflection across the transverse horizontal axis induces a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ grading of the Euclidean algebra, whose odd generators supply charges connecting opposite-parity Cartesian and Bessel modes at equal separation eigenvalues. The Bessel model has an unpaired even zero mode, Witten index one, and unbroken supersymmetry for any rotation-axis position along the reflection line. We express all four separators through mixed supercommutators of displaced orbital-angular-momentum generators, establish Weber pairing through a spectral sign operator, and identify the obstruction to equal-eigenvalue Mathieu pairing at nonzero ellipticity. We extend our construction to multiple transverse shells and generate supersymmetric partner fields with a common Talbot recurrence. Gaussian apodization centered on the rotation axis gives finite-power fields and preserves our charge relations during exact forward propagation while modifying the ideal revival. Our framework may guide optical transformations between parity partners and the characterization of structured fields.

title: Longitudinal-dither wavefront sensing: Calibration-free measurement of mode mismatch
summary: Mode mismatch between a gravitational-wave detector and the beams injected into it lowers the power stored in the arms and the level of squeezing. Correcting it requires the complex amplitudes of the three second-order modes, measured on a calibrated scale with the cavity on resonance at its operating power. Here we present a method that obtains a signal proportional to the mismatch by moving the beam on the wavefront sensors already used for alignment control. A longitudinal dither of the cavity adds to the resonant mode a reference field, which reaches the sensors through the same signal chains and so calibrates both the scale of this signal and the Gouy phases of the sensors and actuators, with no external calibration. We demonstrate the method on an optical cavity held on resonance in its operating state at input powers of 2 W and 62 W. At 2 W it yields an optical model that agrees with independent measurements in the mode content, and with the layout model in the actuator Gouy phase within its uncertainty of about $1^\circ$. At 62 W the thermally induced change of the eigenmode is decomposed into waist-size and waist-position changes. The method requires only components that every controlled cavity already possesses and enables continuous in situ monitoring of the mode matching in the operating state.

title: Recovery of Extended Modes from the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect Due to Local Nonlinearity on a Boundary
summary: Localization in continuum spectra known as the non-Hermitian skin effect is widely believed to be a consequence of nontrivial topology of bulk bands. However, the robustness of the non-Hermitian skin effect against nonlinear effects is still a nontrivial problem. We here reveal that single-bond nonlinearity on a boundary can recover extended modes in a non-Hermitian tight-binding model. We propose and analyze a one-dimensional minimal model, where we introduce a nonlinear phase shift of a hopping term only at boundary sites. We also propose a possible photonic setup to dynamically observe the nonlinearity-induced extended modes as a steady state. Our results thus challenge the conventional notion of the non-Hermitian skin effect by revealing its dependence on nonlinear boundary conditions.

title: Programmable multipartite entanglement analogues
summary: Quantum entanglement underpins the quantum information science. Its multipartite forms distribute coherence across several subsystems, but controlling their composition and order is increasingly difficult as more subsystems participate. Classical nonseparable waves provide accessible analogues of these structures, although existing implementations largely fix the participating degrees of freedom through their generating architectures. Here we overcome this constraint by making multipartiteness itself programmable in electromagnetic fields. A spatiotemporal metasurface reconfigures the identity and number of coherently linked state spaces independently across polarization, frequency, orbital angular momentum, wavevector direction, and orthogonal envelope modes. We realize complete Bell-like and Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-like families from bipartite to five-partite order and exchange constituents at fixed order. To our knowledge, the five-partite state has the highest multipartite order experimentally realized in classical electromagnetic fields. These results establish the distribution of coherence across physical state spaces as a programmable property of classical waves and provide a platform for studying selected structures of multipartite quantum states without invoking quantum entanglement or nonlocality.

title: Observation of programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits
summary: Coherent superposition allows information to be encoded in the geometry of physical states1-7. Preparing individual states, however, does not determine how they can be organized throughout a wave, because the wave propagation and modulation constrain the underlying interference. Here we observe programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits in a space-time metasurface. Coherent synthesis from four discrete responses per polarization channel produces two-component states with the projective geometry of a pure quantum bit. Joint state-space synthesis retains the interference constraints of the shared waveform while allowing distinct polarization states to coexist at different resolved frequencies. Paired spatial and temporal codes organize these states into the prescribed trajectories, reconfigurable Stokes skyrmions and distinct polarizations at 48 experimentally resolved nonzero harmonic orders generated by a shared code pair. This connects the local state preparation to programmable field organization, establishing a physical basis for quantum-inspired information carriers whose encoding can exploit the geometrical paths, spatial winding and coordinated spectral states.

title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
comment: 26 pages, 17 figures, 8 tables. Corrects the analysis of E. O. Silva, Opt. Quantum Electron. 58, 113 (2026), doi:10.1007/s11082-026-08693-8, whose retraction has been requested. Scripts and verification tests are provided as ancillary files
summary: We study the scalar Schrödinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|Ω_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $Δ_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|Ω_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.

title: Reconfigurable Chiral Phonons and Their Selection in Asymmetrically Stacked Graphene MoirMoiré Superlattices
summary: Chiral phonons, lattice vibrations carrying angular momentum, offer a new handle for controlling phonon-mediated phenomena in condensed matter, yet their on-demand generation and deterministic control remain challenging. Here we show, using helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy, that asymmetrically stacked graphene moiré superlattices provide a reconfigurable platform for chiral phonons. We observe a finite degree of circular polarization for both chiral interlayer shear phonons and intralayer optical phonons. A chiral-phonon Raman-tensor model attributes this response to interfacial $C_{2}$-symmetry breaking together with Raman resonance within the van Hove singularity region. Reversing either the twist sense or the stacking order inverts the degree of circular polarization through the spatial transformations linking the corresponding stacking geometries. By tuning the excitation energy and twist angle, we achieve nearly full-range control of the degree of circular polarization of interlayer shear phonons, from $-1$ to $1$, while gate-induced interlayer potential redistribution enables substantial and reversible in situ modulation. These results establish asymmetrically stacked graphene moiré superlattices as a versatile platform for generating and controlling chiral phonons, with implications for optoelectronic and quantum technologies.

title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems
summary: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pmλ_{1},\pmλ_{2}$ satisfying $0<λ_{1} < λ_{2} < 2λ_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.

title: Density-dependent photocarrier recombination in $γ$-InSe
summary: We studied the photocarrier dynamics in $γ$-InSe using femtosecond transient reflectance spectroscopy. By measuring the dependence of the differential reflectance on the injected carrier density, we established an empirical relation between the optical response and carrier density, allowing quantitative analysis of the recombination dynamics. The carrier decay exhibits a strong density dependence, indicating a substantial contribution from nonlinear recombination. At high carrier densities, the dynamics are dominated by a second-order recombination process, with a rate constant of $3.8\times10^{-6}~\mathrm{cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At low densities, the decay becomes approximately exponential, with a carrier lifetime of about 7 ps. We also resolved an initial rise of the band-edge response with a time constant of less than 1 ps, which is attributed to hot-carrier cooling. These results reveal the competition between first-order and second-order recombination in $γ$-InSe and provide quantitative insights into its ultrafast photocarrier dynamics.

title: Non-integer high harmonic generation from many-body nonadiabatic gating
comment: 10 pages main text, 5 figures, 43 pages supplementary information
summary: High harmonic generation (HHG) in solids typically produces a rigid frequency comb locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. In strongly correlated materials, however, the light field can dynamically transform the electronic state on the timescale of harmonic generation itself, potentially violating this rule. Here, we report giant blueshifted, non-integer HHG in a cuprate Mott insulator Sr$_2$CuO$_3$ produced by mid-infrared excitations. Concurrent transient reflectivity measurements and time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model support a many-body temporal gating mechanism that suppresses light emission on the trailing edge of the pulse, thereby blueshifting radiated harmonics in the frequency domain. Our findings establish HHG emission energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many-body dynamics and pave the way for exploration and manipulation of correlated electronic phases of matter with strong-field spectroscopy.

title: Beyond Quantum Mechanics: From Nonlinear to Emergent and Solitonic Approaches
comment: Master's thesis in Physics, Sapienza University of Rome, defended on 17 November 2026. Supervisor: Prof. Claudio Conti. 137 pages
summary:
This thesis investigates the role of nonlinearity in approaches beyond standard quantum mechanics, following a path from modifications of quantum dynamics to the possibility of an emergent statistical description. We first examine Weinberg's nonlinear formulation and its implications for the statistical interpretation of quantum states. We then discuss de Broglie-Bohm theory and the Madelung formulation, which provide a framework for comparing guided trajectories with ensemble descriptions involving momentum fluctuations. The Hall-Reginatto exact uncertainty approach identifies the fluctuation energy associated with the quantum potential.
  We then investigate whether quantum dynamics can emerge from the collective statistics of solitons in a fluctuating background, using a Galilean formulation of the complex sine-Gordon model. Within a weak-noise approximation, we identify a regime in which the statistics of the soliton centres reproduce the Schr{ö}dinger equation, with an effective action scale determined by the background fluctuations. This correspondence is established for Gaussian ensembles and potentials at most quadratic.
  These results provide a concrete setting for exploring how quantum dynamics can emerge as a statistical description of underlying nonlinear field dynamics.

title: Whistler instability driven by electron trapping in magnetic dips
summary: Using fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations, we show how free energy released by an ion-scale instability reaches electron scales through its effect on the electron distribution. An initial ion temperature anisotropy drives partly compressional ion cyclotron waves, which form magnetic dips. Electrons trapped in these dips develop an enhanced temperature anisotropy and butterfly-shaped distributions, similar to those observed by spacecraft in the Earth's magnetosheath. By tracking the energy transfer in velocity space, we show that the gradients created by trapping drive whistler waves through cyclotron resonance. The whistlers in turn scatter the electrons in pitch angle, flattening velocity-space gradients and heating the electrons along the magnetic field. As a result, the electron anisotropy drops to about half of the double-adiabatic prediction once the whistler power peaks. Our results show that it is the shape of the electron distribution in magnetic dips, rather than its temperature anisotropy alone, that drives the whistlers.

title: Annular-curvature effects on high-frequency azimuthal fluctuations in 3D PIC simulations of Hall-thruster plasmas
summary: Azimuthal instabilities and associated plasma fluctuations play an important role in anomalous cross-field electron transport in Hall thrusters. Kinetic studies often approximate the annular discharge using local Cartesian domains, but the influence of the neglected curvature on threedimensional fluctuation dynamics remains insufficiently quantified. Here, three-dimensional cylindrical electrostatic particle-in-cell simulations assess this geometric effect in a reduced channel-plume model by varying the minimum computational-domain radius rmin at fixed channel width and imposed magnetic-field profile. The dominant channel wavenumbers on the centerline-reference scale remain similar, while pronounced radial amplitude asymmetry develops in the smaller-radius configurations. At rmin = 10 cm and 2 cm, the outer-channel electric-field amplitudes in the dominant wavenumber band exceed the inner-channel values by 26% and 53%, respectively. In the plume, low-wavenumber fluctuations favor the inner region, whereas high-wavenumber components favor the outer region. Density-electric-field covariance is preferentially concentrated in the outer channel and inner plume, with outer-to-inner magnitude ratios of 2.71 and 0.58 at rmin = 2 cm. These persistent spatial preferences connect the geometric redistribution of fluctuations to the correlated axial ExB drift contribution. For the 1.28 cm channel width studied, these results support retaining cylindrical geometry at rmin = 10 cm and 2 cm to resolve local fluctuations and transport-related correlations, even when the imposed magnetic-field profile is unchanged.

title: Measuring the tug-of-war between two nonlinearities in a monopolar plasma vortex
summary: From planetary atmospheres to magnetized plasmas, single-core vortices organize flows and transport heat and matter. Understanding their persistence requires identifying the nonlinear interactions that sustain a single core. The Charney--Hasegawa--Mima equation, shared by drift waves and Rossby waves, admits steadily propagating localized vortex solutions only in dipole form. Theories of monopolar drift vortices attribute the additional nonlinearity to either the electron-temperature gradient or density-profile curvature, but their respective roles remain experimentally unresolved. Here we show that the coupling sustaining a monopolar drift vortex results from the near cancellation of two much larger nonlinear contributions. We measure three-wave coupling among the vortex harmonics using simultaneous probe signals acquired around the full azimuth of a laboratory plasma and compare it with predictions of an extended drift-wave equation derived for the measured equilibrium conditions. The equation reproduces the sign, magnitude and triad dependence of the observed coupling without adjustable parameters, whereas neither contribution alone accounts for the measured coupling pattern. This coupling transfers fluctuation power from the linearly driven fundamental to damped harmonics, maintaining the single-core waveform. These results establish an experimental route to distinguishing mechanisms that produce similar vortex structures by resolving the nonlinear interactions within them.

title: Global full-f gyrokinetic analysis of energetic-particle-driven Alfvén eigenmodes and their phase-space drive with GYSELA
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Submitted to Nuclear Fusion
summary: We investigate the linear stability of energetic-particle (EP) driven Alfvén eigenmodes and the wave-particle interaction in phase space, using the newly implemented energetic-particle module in the electromagnetic global full-f gyrokinetic code GYSELA. The coupled gyrokinetic-Maxwell system self-consistently evolves the EP species alongside thermal ions and kinetic electrons, retaining finite-orbit-width and global profile effects. To mitigate the relaxation of the initial distribution in global full-f models, a canonical Maxwellian initialisation is employed, which strongly reduces this relaxation and the associated change of the drive. The framework is verified against the ITPA-TAE and the reversed-shear NLED-AUG cases, including scans in EP temperature and density. The agreement with published multi-code results is quantitative for the ITPA-TAE case and qualitative for the NLED-AUG case, where a reversed-shear Alfvén eigenmode (RSAE) is found near $q_{\rm min}$. Beyond verification, we use a constants-of-motion (CoM) diagnostic to project the gyrocentre distribution and the local wave-particle power exchange ($P = -\mathbf{J}\cdot\mathbf{E}$) onto invariant space. This identifies the orbit classes and resonances that interact with the mode. For the ITPA-TAE, deeply co-passing orbits dominate the drive. For the NLED-AUG RSAE, counter-passing orbits drive the mode and co-passing orbits damp it, and the sign of the exchange follows that of the linear EP drive. These results provide a basis for future global full-f studies of nonlinear energetic-particle transport and mode saturation.

title: The effects of closure parameter on the properties of kinetic range plasma turbulence
summary:
Simulations of plasmas such as the solar wind require an accurate representation of kinetic physics given the lack of frequent collisions. Fully kinetic treatments are computationally expensive and necessarily confine simulations to small domain sizes. A good compromise is to utilise higher-order fluid-moment models such as the 10-moment model.
  This model retains all physics up to the second moment, with the moment hierarchy closed by approximating the heat flux.
  One choice is to use a model for the divergence of the heat flux, $\partial_m q_{ijm} \approx v_t |k_0|(\mathbf{P}_{ij}-pδ_{ij})$, with a free parameter $k_0$, called the ``closure parameter''. We study the effects of this closure parameter on the properties of turbulence, combined with artificial ion-electron mass ratios. We show that the heating of the two plasma species is affected by the choice of the closure parameter. For all combinations of closure parameters, the relative compressive and incompressive heating rates are affected even for realistic mass ratios. The effects are more prominent for lower mass ratios and diminish when approaching realistic mass ratios.

title: Streaming instabilities and electron transport in electron transpiration cooling
summary: Electron transpiration cooling requires emitted electrons to travel through a surrounding plasma, where their relative motion with background electrons can drive streaming instabilities. We investigate these instabilities using particle-in-cell simulations with Monte Carlo collisions in a finite helium plasma. Lower neutral densities show pronounced wave activity, while higher densities give smoother electron distributions. A multifluid model constructed from simulated velocity distributions captures the frequency scale and decay direction in selected cases, but underestimates the separate driving and absorbing responses of electron populations. Distinguishing fast and slow emitted electrons and normalizing the field amplitude by the expanding two-peak length improves the low-wavenumber growth comparison, while discrepancies remain. Spatial growth estimates show that finite propagation distance also limits amplification. Strong late-time current fluctuations can coexist with nearly complete mean anode collection. These findings connect streaming instability to electron transport in the cooling model and show both the usefulness and limitations of a fluid description.

title: Toward divertor plasma detachment in pure D-T plasma in fusion reactor with H-mode-like plasma confinement
summary: The conditions between the separatrix plasma density and the heat flux into the scrape-off layer region allowing reaching an ultimate divertor plasma detachment with H-mode confinement in pure hydrogen (deuterium or the mixture of deuterium and tritium) plasma are obtained. Estimates for a number of present-day tokamaks show that this regime is accessible at separatrix plasma densities below or around the empirical density limit. Moreover, they are in reasonable agreement with the data from the AUG tokamak, where detachment was reached in pure deuterium plasma. However, in future reactors, such as ITER, ARC, and EU-DEMO, it would require densities exceeding this empirical density limit. Therefore, additional measures are needed for future reactors, such as operation above the density limit, which, according to recent experimental data, may not be a hard operational boundary, turbulence induced broadening of the heat flux width and reduction of the parallel heat flux in the long legs of advanced divertor configurations. Their successful implementation would open the possibility for a more efficient reactor design.

title: Exact force-free three-dimensional toroidal equilibria and the sawtooth q(0) problem
summary: We construct exact, closed-form solutions of curl of B=lambda B with nested toroidal flux surfaces around a closed magnetic axis, finite rotational transform and, in general, no continuous Euclidean symmetry. They are counterexamples to Grad's conjecture in its pressureless form. Inside a regular flux surface that fits in a ball of radius r_b with |lambda| r_b<4.49, each is the unique minimum of magnetic energy at fixed toroidal flux and helicity, so each is a Taylor state. The rotational transform is a ratio of one-dimensional integrals. Our primary application is the sawtooth q(0) problem in tokamaks. In one configuration, q crosses unity on a smooth torus of closed field lines, with no island and no current sheet. Across the family, minimum-energy fixed-boundary states with q(0)<1<q_wall exist; in our scans q(0) reaches 0.84 at tight aspect ratio and about 0.94 at conventional aspect ratio. At comparable helicity-to-flux ratio, configurations with different boundary shapes have either sign of the magnetic shear. These fixed-boundary equilibria are candidates for relaxed cores, which need not be axisymmetric. Their dynamical accessibility and their matching to the surrounding plasma remain open.

title: Plasma Heating by Magnetic Reconnection and Alfven Waves in Collisionless Shocks
comment: accepted for publication in Physics of Plasmas
summary: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. In this study, we focus on these large-amplitude Alfven waves and examine not only plasma heating through conventional wave-particle interactions but also preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by trains of such waves. Using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, we find a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region, and we suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence the energy partitioning between ions and electrons.

title: CHORD: Learning Latent Spaces for Constrained Stellarator Design
summary: In high-dimensional, PDE-constrained design, interpolating between known feasible solutions can reveal trade-offs without repeating expensive optimization campaigns. In stellarator design for fusion energy, direct interpolation of plasma boundary parameters can violate physical constraints even when both endpoints are feasible. Learned latent representations can capture nonlinear relationships among design variables, but latent interpolation can still cross infeasible regions, and conditioning on target metrics can become inconsistent with the decoded design. We introduce CHORD, a conditional variational autoencoder that penalizes predicted constraint violations along decoded latent interpolants during training, paired with self-consistent inference that aligns conditioning with the decoded design's predicted metrics. Geometric benchmarks show the benefit of regularizing latent interpolants. In stellarator interpolation between distinct geometry families, CHORD reaches up to 81% simulator-validated mid-segment feasibility, compared with 50% for an unregularized conditional VAE and 28% for direct interpolation of boundary parameters. Ablations show that both ingredients are needed for this gain. Beyond interpolation, latent-space optimization finds simulator-feasible designs, while self-consistent sampling produces more diverse feasible alternatives. On the ConStellaration benchmark, chord-regularized models with linear conditioning reuse data from five optimization campaigns and simulator-labeled rescalings to populate the Pareto front more densely. After low-fidelity screening, 93% of 1.2k generated candidates pass the benchmark's high-fidelity feasibility test. We release code and over 600k designs for stellarator generation, surrogate training, and front-filling evaluation. These results support feasibility-aware latent learning for exploring constrained design trade-offs.

title: Making Reconnection Cooler: A relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics model for radiative collisionless reconnection
summary: Relativistic magnetic reconnection around astrophysical compact objects is a likely site for particle energization and multiwavelength emission. Kinetic theory has substantially modelled such collisionless radiative relativistic reconnection using a radiative drag force countering the acceleration of the particles. Here, we systematically derive an energy-momentum sink term in relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD), informed by kinetic theory and coupled with a charge-starved resistivity prescription which reproduces the fast reconnection rate seen in kinetic calculations, to model radiative losses. We show that our radiative loss term accurately captures important macroscopic properties -- including the temperature in the reconnection layer and the bulk motion energy distribution of the out-flowing plasma -- for inverse Compton cooling applied to two-dimensional RRMHD simulations of a reconnection layer and benchmarked to kinetic simulations. Our results hold in various cooling regimes with a one-to-one mapping to kinetic theory. Our radiative model lays a foundation for future RRMHD simulations of plasma in the relativistic radiative regime, such as in reconnection sites in a local turbulent flow or globally in the magnetospheres of black holes and neutron stars.
